findings.text: ext/Chat/Mic.js:67 (`same_as_last_send`) drops a real follow-up message. `strip_words(prev, t) === ""` is true whenever the earlier message matches the START of the new one. So "Okay." followed within 4 s by "Okay, now delete the branch." scores 0 on the first word and the whole second message is thrown away. The reverse test also drops a shorter repeat ("Yes, do it." then "Yes."). Natural-pause sending splits speech into sentences that often start alike, so this will happen. The duplicate check should compare the WHOLE of both texts: `D[S.length][T.length] / max(len)` ≤ 0.35, instead of reusing the prefix-strip.

There is no requirements.md in ai/2026-10-09/dup-chat-bubbles/. task.jsonl names the brief `owner-words.md`, which is not in the folder either, so this review checks the work against the owner's words quoted in doc/duplicate-bubbles.md and the code comments. The brief should be committed beside the task.

ext/drawer/rail.js:342 changes the phone sheet's visible title from "Ask, by voice" to `this.constructor.name`, which shows the raw class name "DrawerRailSheetChat" to the owner. That is outside the duplicate-bubble fix, and so is the compact CSS at ext/drawer/rail.css:314. If the owner asked for both, the doc should say so; if not, they belong in a separate task.

ext/Chat/Mic.js:74 (`collapse_repeat`) also folds a repeat the owner meant to say ("I said stop, I said stop" becomes "I said stop"). This is probably acceptable, but the doc should list it as a known side effect.

ux/Dictate/chat.js:462 is sound: an adopted echo is retagged, and the later `panel.retag(entry.at, r.at)` at :229 then finds nothing and does nothing (Widget.js:359 returns early). The stream's second call is caught by `own_ats`.
